paper.title: May 2024 Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL Paper 2 TZ2
paper.solution_status: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

Ten students’ phone-use times t (hours) are 0.7, 1.2, 1.9, 4.0, 4.4, 4.5, 4.9, 5.7, 6.5, 11.7.

(a) Find (i) the median; (ii) the interquartile range. [3]

An outlier is below Q₁−1.5×IQR or above Q₃+1.5×IQR.

(b) Show 11.7 is an outlier. [3]
questions.summary: Calculate quartiles and test an outlier.
questions.solution: (a) Median=(4.4+4.5)/2=4.45 h. Q₁=1.9,Q₃=5.7, so IQR=3.8 h. (b) Upper fence=5.7+1.5(3.8)=11.4; since 11.7>11.4, it is an outlier.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 6]

For −1≤x≤0, f(x)=1−x² and g(x)=e^(2x). Their graphs intersect at x=a and x=b, a<b.

(a) Find a and b. [3]

(b) Find the enclosed area. [3]
questions.summary: Find numerical intersections and area between curves.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 5]

[Table: x=5,6,6,8,10; y=9,13,p,q,21, where p,q∈ℤ⁺.]

The regression line of y on x is y=2.1875x+0.6875 and passes through (x̄,ȳ).

(a) Given x̄=7, verify ȳ=16. [1]

(b) Given q−p=3, find p and q. [4]
questions.summary: Use a regression mean point to recover data.
questions.solution: (a) ȳ=2.1875(7)+0.6875=16. (b) Since the mean is 16, 9+13+p+q+21=80, so p+q=37. Together with q−p=3, p=17 and q=20.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

Sound loudness L decibels and intensity I units satisfy L=10log₁₀(I×10¹²). S₁ has intensity 10⁻⁶ and loudness 60 dB. S₂ has twice S₁’s intensity.

(a) State S₂’s intensity. [1]

(b) Determine S₂’s loudness. [2]

Thunder has loudness 115 dB.

(c) Find its intensity I. [3]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

A particle’s velocity is v(t)=1+e^(−t)−e^(−sin(2t)) m s⁻¹ for 0≤t≤2.

(a) Find v(2). [1]

(b) Find the maximum velocity. [2]

(c) Find acceleration when the particle changes direction. [3]
questions.solution: (a) v(2)=−0.996114…≈−0.996 m s⁻¹. (b) Solving v′=0 gives t=0.405833… and v_max=1.18230…≈1.18 m s⁻¹. (c) The direction change has v=0 at t=1.65840…. Evaluating a=v′ there gives −2.53487…≈−2.53 m s⁻².

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 5]

X∼B(n,0.25). Determine the least n such that P(X≥1)>0.99.
questions.solution: P(X≥1)=1−P(X=0)=1−0.75ⁿ. Require 0.75ⁿ<0.01, giving n>ln(0.01)/ln(0.75)=16.0078…. Thus the least integer is n=17 (indeed n=16 gives 0.989977<0.99 and n=17 gives 0.992483>0.99).

7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Carp lengths L cm are normal with mean 45.6 and standard deviation 4.2. Lengths between 41.4 cm and k cm lie within one standard deviation.

(a) Write down k. [2]

(b) Find P(L>48). [2]

(c) 99% of carp have length greater than x cm. Find x. [2]

(d) For a random sample of 100: (i) find the expected number with 40<L<56; (ii) find the probability exactly 95 have 40<L<56. [5]

Lengths are recorded to nearest 0.1 cm.

(e) Find P(a recorded length is 45.6 cm). [3]
questions.summary: Use normal and binomial distributions with rounding.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 15]

A window is a semicircle attached to a rectangle of width 2x m and height h m.

[Diagram: rectangle 2x by h topped by a semicircle of radius x.]

(a) Write area A in terms of x,h. [2]

Let perimeter P=10.

(b) Show h=(1/2)(10−2x−πx). [2]

Clear rectangular glass admits 3 light units/m²; tinted semicircle admits 1 unit/m².

(c) Show L=30x−6x²−(5/2)πx². [4]

(d) (i) Find dL/dx. (ii) Find x maximizing L and justify a maximum. (iii) Find corresponding h. [7]
questions.summary: Optimize a composite window under a perimeter constraint.
questions.solution: (a) A=2xh+(1/2)πx². (b) P=2x+2h+πx=10, giving the result. (c) L=3(2xh)+(1/2)πx²; substitution gives 30x−6x²−(5/2)πx². (d) L′=30−12x−5πx. Thus x=30/(12+5π)=1.08272…≈1.08 m. Since L″=−12−5π<0, this is a maximum. Then h=(10−(2+π)x)/2=2.21654…≈2.22 m.

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 17]

A sprinkler at S waters a circle of radius 20 m. S is 14 m from the straight north–south edge of a path, which intersects the circle at A and B.

[Diagram: circle centred S; vertical path edge is a chord through A above B; perpendicular distance from S to chord is 14 m; SA=20 m.]

(a) Show AB=28.57, correct to four significant figures. [3]

The sprinkler makes one revolution every 16 s.

(b) Show it rotates π/8 radians per second. [1]

Let T be the time [AB] is watered each revolution.

(c) Find T. [4]

During one clockwise revolution, at t=0 water crosses at A; at t seconds it crosses at D, d metres south of A. Let α=AŜD and β=SÂB, in radians.

[Diagram: SA=SD=20 m; D lies on chord/path between A and B; perpendicular distance from S to path is 14 m; α at S and β at A.]

(d) Write α in terms of t. [1]

Given β=0.7754 radians,

(e) use the sine rule in triangle ASD to show d(t)=20sin(πt/8)/sin(2.37−πt/8). [3]

A turtle walks south along the path with g(t)=0.05t²+1.1t+18 metres south of A.

(f) At t=0, state how far south it is from A. [1]

Let w be the distance between turtle and D.

(g) (i) Write w in terms of t using g and d. (ii) Hence find when and where the water first reaches the turtle. [4]
questions.summary: Model rotating-sprinkler geometry and an interception.
questions.solution: (a) Half-chord=√(20²−14²)=√204, so AB=2√204=28.5657…=28.57 m. (b) 2π/16=π/8 rad/s. (c) The watered central angle is 2cos⁻¹(14/20)=1.59080 rad, so T=1.59080/(π/8)=4.05093…≈4.05 s. (d) α=πt/8. (e) ∠ADS=π−β−α≈2.37−α. Sine rule gives d/sinα=20/sin(2.37−α), yielding the model. (f) g(0)=18 m. (g)(i) w(t)=0.05t²+1.1t+18−20sin(πt/8)/sin(2.37−πt/8). (ii) First solve w=0: t=3.34880…≈3.35 s. Then g(t)=22.2444…≈22.2 m south of A.
